title: Rossi Sebastiano 2022 · Expected hand and visuotactile PPS
citation: Rossi Sebastiano et al. (2022). Multisensory-driven facilitation within the peripersonal space is modulated by the expectations about stimulus location on the body. Scientific Reports, 12, 20061.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.sequence: Counterbalance block order across participants and randomize conditions within each task.
published_method.visual: Two 5 mm red LEDs at the two hands, which were 40 cm apart. Flash duration 50 ms. Near and far are defined relative to the stimulated hand.
published_method.tactile: Hand dorsum DS7A 200 µs current pulse, two times each hand’s perception threshold. One of two sites selected randomly.
published_method.allocation: Methods describe 24 trials per tactile condition and 24 visual-only trials per position. Bilateral pooling and block assignment of the 48 visual-only trials remain ambiguous.
published_method.response: Press a right-foot pedal when touch is perceived. Rate tactile intensity from 0–7 after each trial. Ignore visual flashes and keep midline fixation.
published_method.analysis: Compare paired responses to the matched tactile-alone condition, primarily on left-hand trials.
published_method.timing: Flash and electrical pulse have nominally simultaneous onsets in paired trials.

stimulus_type.value: Visuotactile detection and rating with a static red LED flash and transcutaneous electrical touch

implementation_gaps: Requires timed independent LEDs and calibrated left/right electrical stimulation with peripheral output timing verification.
A response workflow must combine a foot-pedal detector with the separate intensity rating. Measured visual–tactile offset, exact LED geometry and delivered trial allocation are unresolved.
